MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a multiple of 5? (1 mark)
   A. 65
   B. 66
   C. 64
   D. 67

2. Which of these is a factor of 12? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 8
   C. 7
   D. 4

3. Round 342 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 350
   B. 300
   C. 330
   D. 340

4. What is the total value of the digit 9 in 3,907? (1 mark)
   A. 90
   B. 9,000
   C. 9
   D. 900

5. Which of these shows 460 in words? (1 mark)
   A. four hundred and six
   B. four hundred and sixty
   C. five hundred and sixty
   D. forty-six

6. Work out 3,425 + 2,318. (1 mark)
   A. 5,743
   B. 5,753
   C. 5,643
   D. 5,733

7. Work out 1,204 + 1,315. (1 mark)
   A. 2,419
   B. 3,519
   C. 2,529
   D. 2,519

8. Work out 7,305 + 2,489. (1 mark)
   A. 9,694
   B. 9,794
   C. 9,804
   D. 9,784

9. Work out 48 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 1,008
   B. 1,018
   C. 998
   D. 144

10. What is 35 × 60? (1 mark)
   A. 95
   B. 21,000
   C. 210
   D. 2,100

11. A packet holds 40 sweets. How many sweets are in 15 packets? (1 mark)
   A. 600 sweets
   B. 580 sweets
   C. 700 sweets
   D. 590 sweets

12. Which number is in the 9 times table? (1 mark)
   A. 75
   B. 74
   C. 72
   D. 71

13. What is 45 ÷ 6? (1 mark)
   A. 8 remainder 3
   B. 7 remainder 3
   C. 6 remainder 9
   D. 7 remainder 4

14. What is 900 ÷ 100? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 90
   C. 9
   D. 900

15. Which fraction of an hour is 30 minutes? (1 mark)
   A. 1/3
   B. 1/4
   C. 3/4
   D. 1/2

16. A rectangle is cut into 10 equal parts and 7 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 7/3
   B. 7/10
   C. 10/7
   D. 3/10

17. What is 3/8 of 40? (1 mark)
   A. 25
   B. 15
   C. 5
   D. 20

18. What is 7/10 of 20? (1 mark)
   A. 14
   B. 2
   C. 6
   D. 16

19. Dan writes some fractions. Which of these is a proper fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 13/6
   B. 4 2/3
   C. 1/2
   D. 8/3

20. Write 0.8 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 8/100
   B. 1/8
   C. 80/10
   D. 8/10

21. In the number 8.30, the digit 3 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Hundredths
   B. Tenths
   C. Ones
   D. Tens

22. Which is the largest number: 2.5, 2.05, 2.55, 2.505? (1 mark)
   A. 2.505
   B. 2.5
   C. 2.55
   D. 2.05

23. Simplify 4b + 3b. (1 mark)
   A. 12b
   B. 7
   C. 43b
   D. 7b

24. What is 5 m 20 cm − 2 m 75 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 45 cm
   B. 2 m 55 cm
   C. 2 m 45 cm
   D. 2 m 35 cm

25. What is half a metre in centimetres? (1 mark)
   A. 500 cm
   B. 20 cm
   C. 5 cm
   D. 50 cm

26. What is 4 m 60 cm + 1 m 75 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 6 m 25 cm
   B. 5 m 35 cm
   C. 7 m 35 cm
   D. 6 m 35 cm

27. A triangle has sides of 10 cm, 12 cm and 15 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 39 cm
   B. 38 cm
   C. 37 cm
   D. 44 cm

28. The relationship between metres and centimetres is (1 mark)
   A. 1 m = 100 cm
   B. 1 cm = 100 m
   C. 1 m = 10 cm
   D. 1 m = 1,000 cm

29. A cuboid is 2 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 8 blocks
   B. 6 blocks
   C. 4 blocks
   D. 10 blocks

30. A shop sells 3 packets of milk of 1/2 L each. What is the total amount of milk? (1 mark)
   A. 1 L
   B. 1 1/2 L
   C. 2 L
   D. 3 L

31. How many half-litre containers fill 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 4
   C. 2
   D. 1

32. What is 10 L − 4 1/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 6 L
   B. 5 1/2 L
   C. 5 3/4 L
   D. 6 1/4 L

33. Change 72 hours to days. (1 mark)
   A. 1.2 days
   B. 4 days
   C. 6 days
   D. 3 days

34. Change 90 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 2 h
   B. 1 h 30 min
   C. 2 h 30 min
   D. 1 h

35. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 3 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 12. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 12:15
   B. 3:12
   C. 4:00
   D. 3:00

36. How long is a lesson that starts at 7:40 a.m. and ends at 9:10 a.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 1 h 30 min
   B. 1 h 15 min
   C. 2 h 30 min
   D. 1 h 40 min

37. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 8 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 10. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 8:10
   B. 8:50
   C. 9:50
   D. 10:40

38. Which of these is a right angle? (1 mark)
   A. A half-open pair of scissors
   B. The point of a sharp pencil
   C. The corner of a page in an exercise book
   D. A wide open gate

39. Which statement about a square is true? (1 mark)
   A. It has no lines of symmetry
   B. All four sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   C. Its opposite sides are different
   D. It has only three corners

40. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. How many are matatu or lorry together? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 8
   C. 6
   D. 5

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Find the area of a square with 6 rows of 6 unit squares. Then find the area of a rectangle with 5 rows of 7 squares. Which is bigger? (4 marks)

42. The minute hand of a clock points to 4 and the hour hand is just past 9. What time is it? Explain how you know. (3 marks)

43. 45 eggs are packed in trays that hold 6 eggs each. How many trays are needed to pack all the eggs? Explain. (3 marks)

44. Start at 10,000 and subtract 1,500 each time. Write the first five numbers of the pattern. (3 marks)

45. A bicycle costs Ksh 6,500, a helmet Ksh 1,750 and a lock Ksh 850. Find the total cost. (3 marks)

46. Wangari buys 24 exercise books at Ksh 18 each. Estimate the total cost by rounding to the nearest ten, then work out the exact cost. (4 marks)

47. An L-shaped garden has sides of 6 m, 2 m, 3 m, 2 m, 3 m and 4 m. Find its perimeter. (3 marks)

48. A mother buys 3/4 kg of tomatoes and 1/2 kg of onions. Find the total mass. (3 marks)

49. State two things that are the same and two things that are different about a square and a rectangle. (4 marks)

50. Describe the difference between a clockwise and an anticlockwise turn. (2 marks)

51. Find the volume of a cuboid that is 6 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. Show your working. (3 marks)

52. A tank holds 20 L of water. In the morning 4 1/2 L is taken out and in the afternoon 3 3/4 L is taken out. How much water is left in the tank? (5 marks)

53. Explain how to prepare a shopping list of three items and find its total cost. (4 marks)

54. A shop buys 24 boxes of pencils. Each box has 36 pencils. (a) Estimate the number of pencils by rounding to the nearest ten. (b) Work out the exact number of pencils. (5 marks)

55. Kamau buys 15 packets of sweets and each packet has 40 sweets. How many sweets does he have? (2 marks)

56. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. (a) How many lines of symmetry does it have? (b) How many right angles does it have? (c) Find its perimeter. (d) Say one way in which it is different from a square. (5 marks)

57. List four materials you could use to collect and record data about the types of vehicles that pass the school gate. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 65
   65 = 5 × 13, so 65 is a multiple of 5.

2. D — 4
   12 ÷ 4 = 3 with nothing left over, so 4 is a factor of 12. The others leave a remainder.

3. D — 340
   Look at the ones digit 2. It is less than 5, so keep the tens digit. 342 rounds to 340.

4. D — 900
   The digit 9 is in the hundreds place, so its total value is 9 × 100 = 900.

5. B — four hundred and sixty
   460 = four hundred and sixty. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

6. A — 5,743
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 3,425 + 2,318 = 5,743.

7. D — 2,519
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 1,204 + 1,315 = 2,519.

8. B — 9,794
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 7,305 + 2,489 = 9,794.

9. A — 1,008
   48 × 1 = 48 and 48 × 20 = 960. 48 + 960 = 1,008.

10. D — 2,100
   35 × 6 = 210, then × 10 gives 2,100.

11. A — 600 sweets
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 600 sweets.

12. C — 72
   9 × 8 = 72. The digits of a multiple of 9 add up to 9: 7 + 2 = 9.

13. B — 7 remainder 3
   6 × 7 = 42 and 45 − 42 = 3. So 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3. Check: 7 × 6 + 3 = 45.

14. C — 9
   Dividing by 100 removes two zeros. 900 ÷ 100 = 9.

15. D — 1/2
   There are 60 minutes in an hour. 30 minutes is half of 60, so it is 1/2 of an hour.

16. B — 7/10
   The whole has 10 equal parts and 7 are shaded, so 7/10 is shaded.

17. B — 15
   40 ÷ 8 = 5 and 5 × 3 = 15. So 3/8 of 40 is 15.

18. A — 14
   20 ÷ 10 = 2 and 2 × 7 = 14. So 7/10 of 20 is 14.

19. C — 1/2
   In a proper fraction the numerator is smaller than the denominator, so 1/2 is less than one whole.

20. D — 8/10
   The last digit of 0.8 is in the tenths place, so the denominator is 10. 0.8 = 8/10.

21. B — Tenths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 8.30 the digit 3 is in the tenths place.

22. C — 2.55
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The largest number is 2.55.

23. D — 7b
   Only like terms can be joined. 4b + 3b = 7b.

24. C — 2 m 45 cm
   520 − 275 = 245 cm = 2 m 45 cm.

25. D — 50 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: half a metre in centimetres is 50 cm.

26. D — 6 m 35 cm
   Change to centimetres: 460 + 175 = 635 cm = 6 m 35 cm.

27. C — 37 cm
   Add all three sides: 10 + 12 + 15 = 37 cm.

28. A — 1 m = 100 cm
   There are 100 centimetres in one metre.

29. A — 8 blocks
   One layer has 2 × 2 = 4 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 4 × 2 = 8 blocks.

30. B — 1 1/2 L
   3 × 1/2 = 3/2 = 1 1/2 L.

31. C — 2
   Two halves make one whole.

32. C — 5 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 10 L − 4 1/4 L = 5 3/4 L.

33. D — 3 days
   72 ÷ 24 = 3 days.

34. B — 1 h 30 min
   90 ÷ 60 = 1 remainder 30, so 90 minutes = 1 h 30 min.

35. D — 3:00
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 12 shows 12 × 5 = 0 minutes, so the time is 3:00.

36. A — 1 h 30 min
   Count on from 7:40 a.m. to 9:10 a.m.. The total is 1 h 30 min.

37. B — 8:50
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 10 shows 10 × 5 = 50 minutes, so the time is 8:50.

38. C — The corner of a page in an exercise book
   A page corner is a square corner, which is a right angle.

39. B — All four sides are equal and all corners are right angles
   A square has four equal sides and four right angles.

40. C — 6
   5 + 1 = 6.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Square 36, rectangle 35. The square is bigger by 1 square unit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each area and 1 mark for the comparison and 1 mark for the difference.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9:20. Each number is worth 5 minutes, so the minute hand at 4 shows 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past 9.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 9:20, 1 mark for 5 minutes per number, 1 mark for 4 × 5.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 8 trays
   Working / marking points: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3 (1 mark). Seven trays are full (1 mark). The 3 left-over eggs need another tray, so 8 trays (1 mark).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000, 8,500, 7,000, 5,500, 4,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct rule and 2 marks for the numbers.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 9,100
   Working / marking points: 6,500 + 1,750 = 8,250 (1 mark); 8,250 + 850 (1 mark); Ksh 9,100 (1 mark).

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 20 × 20 = 400. Exact: 24 × 18 = 432 shillings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 400, 1 mark for the exact working (24 × 8 = 192 and 24 × 10 = 240), 1 mark for 432.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20 m
   Working / marking points: 6 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 20 m. 2 marks for adding all six sides, 1 mark for the unit.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 1/4 kg
   Working / marking points: 3/4 + 1/2 = 3/4 + 2/4 (1 mark); = 5/4 (1 mark); = 1 1/4 kg (1 mark).

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Same: both have four straight sides and four right angles. Different: a square has all four sides equal and 4 lines of symmetry, but a rectangle has only opposite sides equal and 2 lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for two similarities and 2 marks for two differences.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: A clockwise turn goes the same way as the hands of a clock. An anticlockwise turn goes the opposite way.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: 72 blocks
   Working / marking points: 6 × 4 = 24 blocks in a layer (1 mark); 24 × 3 (1 mark); 72 blocks (1 mark).

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: 11 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Total taken: 4 1/2 + 3 3/4 = 4 2/4 + 3 3/4 = 7 5/4 = 8 1/4 L (3 marks). 20 − 8 1/4 = 11 3/4 L (2 marks).

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide what is needed, write the three items with numbers, find the price of each, work out the cost of each item, and add the costs to get the total.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for choosing items, 1 mark for writing quantity, 1 mark for prices, 1 mark for adding the costs.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 20 × 40 = 800 (b) 864 pencils
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding both numbers, 1 mark for 800, 2 marks for 36 × 4 = 144 and 36 × 20 = 720, 1 mark for 864.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: 600 sweets
   Working / marking points: 15 × 4 = 60 (1 mark), then × 10 = 600 (1 mark).

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 2 (b) 4 (c) 26 cm (d) Its sides are not all equal (only opposite sides are equal), and it has 2 lines of symmetry instead of 4.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for (a), 1 mark for (b), 2 marks for (c) (8 + 5 + 8 + 5 with the answer and unit), 1 mark for (d).

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: a pencil, an exercise book or paper, a ruler for drawing a table, a clipboard or hard book, a watch or clock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible material.
